name: Guided by Voices
label: Matador
lede: A Dayton fourth-grade teacher who once pitched a college no-hitter spent a decade making four-track records almost nobody heard. Then he got discovered, quit the classroom, and has now put out 44 albums as Guided by Voices.

eras.title: A teacher's band nobody outside Dayton heard
eras.text: Robert Pollard taught fourth grade in Dayton, Ohio, and led a bar band that drifted into his basement. For nearly a decade Guided by Voices paid to press records in runs of a few hundred, and almost nobody bought them.

years.src: Wikipedia: Robert Pollard · Wikipedia: Guided by Voices · BrooklynVegan
years.h: [[Robert Pollard|e7f29e49-6078-4528-a5dc-5d0eeb8a1437]] swaps the mound for fourth grade and a bar band
years.p: Pollard pitched a no-hitter for Wright State, then settled into teaching. His brother Jim Pollard, Mitch Mitchell and Kevin Fennell make up the first Guided by Voices line-up.
years.xp:
Pollard has said he quit sports because he was "sick of people snapping their fingers and expecting me to move." He taught for 14 years, at every primary level before landing on fourth grade, and spent the vacations on music. "I never went to the teachers' lounge," he has said. "But the teachers liked me."

School leaked into the songs, including Gold Star for Robot Boy and Teenage FBI. Pollard now has nearly 3,000 songs registered with BMI.

The earliest known live footage of the band, on the photo above, is a 16-song, 40-plus-minute set at the Dayton Riverfest bandshell on May 26, 1986, shot for local public access TV. It came out on the DVD Thank You Very Much for Absolutely Nothing, limited to 1,000 copies.

years.h: [[Tobin Sprout|4b05ba8c-0f7b-4735-b8c1-153a5875a4d8]] brings a second set of songs and a home studio
years.p: An Ohio University-trained illustrator, Sprout joins as guitarist, engineer and the band's second songwriter.

years.h: The band pays to press Devil Between My Toes and Sandbox
years.p: After the EP Forever Since Breakfast, Guided by Voices finances its own albums and presses only a few hundred of each. Self-Inflicted Aerial Nostalgia and Same Place the Fly Got Smashed follow.

years.src: Wikipedia: Propeller · Wikipedia: Guided by Voices
years.h: Propeller is meant as a goodbye, in 500 handmade sleeves
years.p: Deep in debt, Robert Pollard planned it as the last Guided by Voices record. Each of the 500 copies got a one-off cover of paint, screen prints and found objects.
years.xp:
The roar of G-B-V! that opens the record was faked in the studio: the band had barely played live. Fans have chanted it at shows ever since, and the band recreated the whole opening at its 2004 final show. By 2005, original sleeves reportedly sold for thousands of dollars.

College radio, and praise from [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]], [[R.E.M.|ea4dfa26-f633-4da6-a52a-f49ea4897b58]] and [[The Breeders|667e856e-f3a7-42e9-8244-95422ef31321]], carried the record out of Dayton.

years.h: Robert Pollard calls it quits and teaches full-time
years.p: He ends the band after Propeller. The breakup doesn't stick: by 1993 Guided by Voices is back.

eras.title: Bee Thousand makes them a cause
eras.text: The line-up of Pollard, Sprout, Mitchell, Greg Demos and Kevin Fennell played outside Ohio for the first time. Bee Thousand turned them into an indie-rock cause, Matador signed them, and Pollard left teaching.

years.h: Vampire on Titus is named for the street where Pollard lived
years.p: Made by just Robert Pollard, Jim Pollard and Tobin Sprout, it is often called the harshest lo-fi record in the catalog.
years.xp: Jim Shepard of V-3 once told Pollard he pulled songs out of the ground like a vampire on Titus, the Dayton avenue where Pollard lived. Scat released it, with Propeller appended.

years.h: The classic five leave Ohio for New York and Philadelphia
years.p: With Robert Pollard, Tobin Sprout, Mitch Mitchell, Greg Demos and Kevin Fennell, Guided by Voices plays outside its home state for the first time.

years.h: Bee Thousand was supposed to be the last one
years.p: Built mostly from old songs on Portastudios in Dayton garages and basements, with the mistakes left in. Pitchfork later ranked it No. 10 of the 1990s.
years.xp:
Pollard was thinking about ending the band over money. His reasoning: if nobody was listening anyway, "I'm going to put exactly what I want on them." The album was recorded over three days, most songs took about 30 minutes with no rehearsal, and the guitar drops out on Hardcore UFO's and Mincer Ray.

The cover comes from a National Geographic story on Mardi Gras in Acadiana. The title mixes a mile marker, Z1000 or zoo thousand, with a misspelled Beethoven. In 2009 Amazon ranked it No. 1 on its list of the 100 greatest indie rock albums.

years.h: Robert Pollard leaves teaching for good, and labels start calling
years.p: Guided by Voices signs with Matador as Pollard and his bandmates retire from their day jobs to do music full-time.

years.big: "If you leave out the beer, was about ten dollars"
q: The cost for recording Alien Lanes, if you leave out the beer, was about ten dollars.
James Greer, in his history of the band
years.h: Matador advances nearly $100,000 for Alien Lanes
years.p: It was one of the label's biggest deals then, and the band made all 27 songs at Tobin Sprout's home studio in Dayton.
years.xp:
The album came out April 4, 1995, 27 tracks in 41 minutes. Pitchfork gave it 9.2 and put it at No. 27 in its top 100 of the 1990s; Magnet named it album of 1995. Robert Christgau gave it a "dud."

James Greer, who played bass in the band in the mid-1990s, later wrote its history.

years.h: Motor Away becomes the Alien Lanes single
years.p: Matador releases it on June 6, two months after the album. Below, the band at Cat's Cradle in Chapel Hill six weeks later.

years.src: Wikipedia: Under the Bushes Under the Stars
yt: Full show, Whisky a Go Go, May 10, 1996
years.h: Under the Bushes Under the Stars leaves the four-track behind
years.p: Guided by Voices moves into 24-track studios, with [[Kim Deal|760e4df4-e851-46c8-b34d-afa2e9706831]] and [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] among the producers, but Robert Pollard still sings through guitar amps.
years.xp:
Sessions ran through at least four studios and several producer teams, including John Shough, Doug Easley and Davis McCain. The last six songs weren't in the original sequence; Matador's executives asked for them, and the vinyl edition put them on a separate 12-inch EP.

Reviews ran from NME's 8/10 and Entertainment Weekly's B+ to Spin's 6/10. It was the last classic-line-up album until Let's Go Eat the Factory in 2012.

years.src: Wikipedia: Guided by Voices · Wikipedia: Tobin Sprout
years.h: Sprout steps off the road, and two solo albums arrive the same day
years.p: Tobin Sprout stops touring to raise his first child, paint and make solo records. His Carnival Boy and Robert Pollard's Not in My Airforce come out the same day, each man playing on the other's.
years.xp: Sprout went on to paint and publish children's books; Tim Allen has said he collects Sprout's artwork. Sprout and Pollard later worked together again as Airport 5 in 2001.

eras.title: Pollard keeps the name and changes everything else
eras.text: He hired Cleveland's Cobra Verde, then built a harder-rocking band around Doug Gillard. A Ric Ocasek-produced album aimed at radio missed, the shows ran past three hours, and in 2004 Pollard called time.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mag Earwhig! · Wikipedia: Guided by Voices
years.h: Pollard keeps the name and hires Cobra Verde as his band
years.p: [[Doug Gillard|e1cfd005-e293-4196-af38-3a0ac0ab1dbe]] is among the Cleveland players on Mag Earwhig!. The classic line-up appears one last time, on Jane of the Waking Universe, and the Guided by Verde line-up splits late in 1997.
years.xp: Most tracks were cut in professional studios in Cleveland, a step away from the four-track sound; more material was recorded in Dayton at Cro-Magnon Studios in 1997. NME gave it 6/10, Pitchfork 8.0.

years.h: [[Ric Ocasek|697d4510-c3fe-4e96-bcc9-34739bccde8f]] polishes Do the Collapse, and radio passes
years.p: Made for Capitol but released on TVT, the album is slick and heavily processed. Reviews are mixed and there is no radio breakthrough.

years.h: Sets often run past three hours
years.p: The band plays new songs, classics, Robert Pollard solo tracks and covers of [[The Who|9fdaa16b-a6c4-4831-b87c-bc9ca8ce7eaa]], David Bowie and [[The Rolling Stones|b071f9fa-14b0-4217-8e97-eb41da73f598]], with the drinking never stopping. In 2000 the tour reaches Japan and New Zealand.

years.h: Pollard opens the vault with Suitcase, 100 songs on four discs
years.p: The box set collects 100 unreleased songs spanning three decades.

years.h: Back on Matador, and back to the mid-1990s sound
years.p: Universal Truths and Cycles arrives after Guided by Voices leaves TVT, with Todd Tobias producing.

years.big: "This feels like the last album for Guided by Voices."
q: This feels like the last album for Guided by Voices.
years.h: Half Smiles of the Decomposed is billed as the last Guided by Voices album
years.p: Robert Pollard had always said a final-album record would end the band, and he says this is it.

years.h: Four weeks before the end, Guided by Voices plays Conan
years.p: The band performs Everybody Thinks I'm a Raincloud (When I'm Not Looking) on Late Night with Conan O'Brien.

years.src: Wikipedia: Guided by Voices · Wikipedia: Propeller
years.h: Guided by Voices ends on New Year's Eve with 63 songs at the Metro
years.p: The four-hour finale in Chicago is released on DVD as The Electrifying Conclusion.
years.xp: The band recreated the entire opening of Propeller for the finale, studio-made G-B-V chant included.

eras.title: The classic five come back
eras.text: Matador's 21st birthday reunited the 1993–96 line-up, and six albums followed in three years. It ended over a drum kit and a Facebook post.

years.h: The classic line-up plays Matador at 21 in Las Vegas
years.p: Announced in June, the 1993–96 line-up takes the label's 21st anniversary weekend. The tour that follows sells out nearly every date, Maxwell's in Hoboken included.

years.h: First album from the classic line-up since 1996
years.p: Let's Go Eat the Factory opens the reunion's run of records. Class Clown Spots a UFO follows June 12, and The Bears for Lunch in November.

years.h: Kevin Fennell puts the Bee Thousand drum kit up for $55,000
years.p: The drummer tries to sell the kit used on Bee Thousand and other albums. Robert Pollard says he fired Fennell; Fennell says he quit.
years.xp: The dispute went public on October 23, 2013, when Pitchfork reported it.

years.h: Kevin March replaces Fennell behind the drums on Cool Planet
years.p: It is the sixth album of the reunion. Motivational Jumpsuit came out in February.

years.h: A Facebook statement ends the reunion, tour dates and all
years.p: On September 18, Guided by Voices abruptly announces it has disbanded again. The remaining tour dates are canceled.

eras.title: The albums keep coming, the touring stops
eras.text: Pollard brought the name back with a new band built around Doug Gillard and Kevin March, and the albums kept coming. By 2025 he had decided he was too old to tour.

years.h: A Sled Island headline slot announces the comeback
years.p: Calgary's festival gets the band on June 25, and a new album, Please Be Honest, on which Robert Pollard plays every instrument. Bobby Bare Jr. and Mark Shue join.

years.cap: Guided by Voices at the GARP music festival, September 2016
years.h: Nick Mitchell is fired in the Grog Shop dressing room
years.p: After a set at the Grog Shop in Cleveland, the guitarist is let go on the spot. Doug Gillard replaces him and rejoins for good later that month.

years.h: Pollard's 100th album is a double, August by Cake
years.p: By the count Wikipedia cites, it is Robert Pollard's 100th release across his bands and solo work. How Do You Spell Heaven follows in August.

years.h: Pollard won't tour album 44, Thick Rich and Delicious
years.p: Guided by Voices releases its 44th album, and Robert Pollard says the band won't take it out: "I feel too old to get onstage."

years.h: Album 45 is called Crawlspace of the Pantheon
years.p: Guided by Voices announces a May 29, 2026 release, led by the single We Outlast Them All.
